PART A – DESIGN (25 Marks)
TASK A1 – Model the City as a Graph
A1.1 – Identify the Graph
A1.2 – Choose the Representation
A1.3 – Handle Change
Alternative: Adjacency Matrix
TASK A2 – Design the Traversals
A2.1 – BFS and DFS
A2.2 – Choose the Traversal
A2.3 – Trace on a Seven-Vertex Example
Predict the Output – Given DFS Program
Alternative: Iterative DFS
TASK A3 – Design the Topological Order
A3.1 – Model the Dependencies
A3.2 – Kahn’s Algorithm and DFS Algorithm
A3.3 – Many Valid Orders
Complete Code – Kahn’s Algorithm
Alternative: DFS Topological Sort
TASK A4 – Design the Shortest-Path Strategy
A4.1 – Dijkstra versus Floyd–Warshall
A4.2 – Limits and AI Pathfinding
Predict the Output – Floyd–Warshall Program
Alternative: Run Dijkstra from Each Hub
TASK A5 – Design the Minimum Spanning Tree
A5.1 – Prim’s Algorithm
A5.2 – MST versus Shortest Paths
Complete Code – Prim’s Algorithm
Alternative: Kruskal’s Algorithm
PART B – IMPLEMENTATION & EXPERIMENTAL INVESTIGATION (25 Marks)
Common Compilation and Testing
TASK B1 – Implement and Validate the Traversals
B1.1 – Completed BFS Program (CSR Adjacency List)
B1.2 – Compare with Part A
B1.3 – Connected Components and Cycles
B1.4 – Matrix versus List
TASK B2 – Engineer Difficult Inputs for Dijkstra
Completed Dijkstra Program
Difficult Input Tests and Findings
Alternative: Bellman–Ford
TASK B3 – Compare the Shortest-Path Algorithms
B3.1 – Correctness on Eight Vertices
B3.2 – Increase the Data Size
B3.3 – A* on a Grid
B3.4 – Engineering Trade-Off
TASK B4 – Final Engineering Decision
B4.1 – Practical MST Extension
B4.2 – Check Scalability
B4.3 – Production Decision
Alternative: Precompute Major-Junction Paths
